conventions.convention: Countable Choice is assumed; full Choice and existence of an ambient Hilbert basis are not assumed. Singular-value sums start at n=1. Every displayed index operator must have a bounded trace-class extension from its specified dense domain.

An oriented ij trajectory has Im(exp(-iθW)(λ(i)-λ(j))(ż))=0 and positive corresponding real part; orientation reversal exchanges ij and ji. The network phase θW and interface phase θfr are independent unless the model relates them.
Physical charges form a model-specified quotient of a subgroup of geometric homology. The physical period normalization ZT(ρ(γ))=π⁻¹∫γλ is conditional on periods vanishing on ker ρ.

GMN edge length integrates the sheet difference; KT edge length integrates the cover one-form. For the stated cubic sheet pair, LGMN=√3 LKT. Physical GMN string mass uses LGMN/π with a physical mass-dimension-one differential.

The framed formula uses J=2J12+2I12, a model-specified power convention for (-y)^J, admissible y-values, and a fixed fermion-number/sign refinement. Its y=1 specialization is distinguished from the monograph's trace exp(iπF) convention.

At source scale α=1, ω=exp(2πi/3), β=∫₀¹x^(-2/3)(1-x)^(-2/3)dx, a=(1-ω)β, and λgeom=a dw. The unit-lattice segment has angle π/6, actual KT phase 0, and sheet-difference phase -π/6. The explicit cycle is p-τ(p), with both paths directed from A to B.

load_bearing.statement: For geometric periods use Zgeom(γ)=∫γλ. The physical central charge is a model-supplied group homomorphism ZT:ΓT→(ℂ,+) of mass dimension one. The selected GMN normalization ZT(ρ(γ))=π⁻¹∫γλ for γ∈Γ₀ is available only when ∫κλ=0 for every κ∈ker ρ.

concerns.concern: The Definition combines support K={x²=x³=0}, split into x¹<0 and x¹>0 surface strata, with J=2J12+2I12 and explicitly identifies J12 as rotations in the spatial 1–2 plane. Such rotations move that support: (x¹,0,0) becomes (x¹ cos θ,x¹ sin θ,0). Thus the stated spatial generator does not act as a symmetry on the fixed-defect Hilbert sector without additional transport data. Internal R-symmetry does not restore the moved support. This mixes two source coordinate conventions: [GMN §3.3](https://arxiv.org/html/1204.4824#S3.SS3) uses surface half-lines along x³ with the transverse generator J12; the monograph's §22.3.1 uses x¹ supports but gives an unrefined trace without this rotation insertion. The physical framed-index convention needs a consistent support/generator identification; trace-class assumptions alone do not provide it.

Example paragraph beginning 'For the separate defect-index convention' imports J=2J12+2I12 from the assigned definition, including its incompatible x¹-supported defect arrangement and spatial 1–2 rotation interpretation. This consumer needs checking when that supplier convention is resolved. The defect-index issue does not affect the verified geometric cycle, period, phase, metric calculation, or correctly placed torus diagram.

The sentence 'Genericity excludes any nonzero bulk or relative central charge on the forbidden ray' does not define a relative central-charge map or identify the relative sectors being quantified over. Earlier ZT is defined only on the absolute physical charge group. [GMN §3.3](https://arxiv.org/html/1204.4824#S3.SS3) tests the endpoint soliton sectors Γ(z₁,z₁) and Γ(z₂,z₂), in addition to bulk charges. Specify these domains and the model-supplied relative central charges, including compatibility with absolute-charge translations and any adopted period normalization.

seams_checked.note: Checked the prerequisite page's pure-SU(2) charge/index interface and conditional Hall transport statement against the consumer. The spectral-network definition independently supplies general class-S charge data and does not import the SU(2) lattice, √2 normalization, Hall bridge, or wall-crossing conclusion as universal class-S facts. This is contextual page ordering, without a current item-level invocation of the Hall theorem.

The consumer uses the supplier's general insertion/network data, retains closed total support and complete junction labels, and explicitly declines to assume topologicality. Its open half-planes are strata of one closed network rather than separate closed insertions. It does not import codimension-one topological-interface or fusion properties into the surface-defect interface.
